title: Change in Right Ventricular Strain after Cone Reconstruction of Ebstein’s Anomaly: A Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance-Feature Tracking Study
content: Background. CMR Feature Tracking (CMR-FT) is a well-established method to assess myocardial contraction with diagnostic and prognostic value in many diseases. We aimed to evaluate the role of right ventricular (RV) CMR-FT in perioperative assessment of Ebstein patients undergoing Cone repair. Methods. We analysed CMR data of 18 Ebstein patients before and after Cone repair including CMR-FT derived global radial (GRS), global circumferential (GCS) and global longitudinal strain (GLS). Results. Following Cone repair, tricuspid regurgitation decreased from 48% to 6%, p = 0.0001. RV ejection fraction decreased from 51% to 33%, p = 0.0002, and indexed RV stroke volumes decreased from 74 ml/m² to 43 ml/m², p = 0.0013. GLS decreased from -15.01% to -14.53%, p = 0.0155. GRS and GCS improved from 15.00% to 17.83%, p = 0.0202, and from -8.82% to -13.02%, p = 0.0026. Indexed RV end-diastolic volumes (RVEDVi) decreased, although not significantly, from 161 ml/m2 to 122 ml/m2, p = 0.3465. Eight patients exhibited higher RVEDVi after surgery. Conclusions. Postoperative decrease in RV GLS might be affected by multiple factors such as increased postoperative afterload. RV GCS and GRS might serve as more independent parameters of myocardial function.
